summary: Sustained 5xx spike on AtlasAI tenant after Fluent Bit backlog saturated node I/O causing runtime page-faults and restarts
description:
Issue summary:
Customer AtlasAI reported a sudden, sustained increase in 5xx responses across generation and streaming endpoints beginning ~2026-03-14T10:12Z. Errors were observed for ~20 minutes and correlated with elevated host disk iowait and multiple serving-runtime restarts.

Impact:
- Enterprise customer (AtlasAI) observed 30-40% request failure rate for streaming sessions and short generations.
- Customers reported timeouts and half-closed streaming sessions which required client-side reconnects.
- Business impact: degraded revenue features for AtlasAI; ticket opened by CS for immediate mitigation.

Environment:
- Deployment: Dedicated private cluster for AtlasAI (enterprise).
- Region: prod us-east-1.
- Routing: gateway -> per-tenant edge proxy -> serving-runtime pool pinned to tenant.
- Observability/log pipeline: Fluent Bit forwarder on each node collecting runtime logs and forwarding to CloudLog as well as async archival to S3.

Steps to reproduce (observed / attempted):
1) Customer enabled increased log retention/archival rule via Console around 09:58Z (rotate + forward extra metadata).
2) Fluent Bit on a subset of nodes started queuing backlog (visible in forwarder metrics).
3) Disk write queue length and iowait increased on nodes hosting the serving-runtime for the tenant.
4) Serving runtime experienced repeated page-fault slowdowns and watchdog-triggered restarts; API gateway received upstream connection errors, returned 502/503/504.
5) After throttling the forwarder and draining queues, serving-runtimes stabilized and 5xx rate returned to baseline.

Observed logs / snippets:
- Fluent Bit forwarder backlog metrics: queued_records: ~120k, flush_time_ms median rising to 2.1s
- Node metrics: iowait 80-92%, disk queue length > 50, write latency > 150ms
- dmesg snippets: "page allocation failure" followed by "oom-killer invoked" (note: OOM killer targeted background process initially, but high page-faults caused runtime delays)
- Serving-runtime logs: frequent watchdog timeouts, repeated "runtime heartbeat missed" and graceful exit sequences then immediate reconnection attempts from API gateway.

Initial hypothesis:
- Heavy log-forwarder backlog increased sync disk pressure on shared ephemeral volumes. Serving-runtime experienced blocking page-faults (cold pages + heavy writeback), causing long GC/stop-the-world-like stalls or watchdogesque restarts which manifested as upstream 5xx responses at the gateway.

Immediate mitigation performed:
- Support throttled Fluent Bit forwarders for AtlasAI (reduced target throughput to 20% of previous rate).
- Scaled ephemeral storage IOPS on affected nodes (increase EBS GP3 baseline temporarily) for fastest relief.
- Rebooted two most-impacted runtimes gracefully to clear heavy page caches and resume healthy operation.

Current status:
- 5xx rate reduced to baseline after mitigations at ~2026-03-14T10:35Z. Customer monitoring and CS confirmed degraded behavior resolved. Engineering continues investigation for permanent fix and guardrails.

investigation_notes: Fluent Bit metrics show backlog growth coincident with increased retention rules pushed by customer via Console.
Node-level metrics correlate queued log writes with sustained high iowait and write latency; writeback rate saturation suspected.

dmesg contains page allocation failures and transient OOM-like messages; however OOM targeted background tasks not runtime process. Heavy page-faults prolonged runtime scheduling and triggered watchdog restarts.
API Gateway error patterns: upstream connection reset and 502/503 bursts aligned with runtime heartbeat misses; no abnormal rate limiting on gateway observed.
No evidence of model-level throttling or model kernel faults; serving runtime process was responsive but blocked due to kernel IO stalls.
resolution:
Temporary: Throttled Fluent Bit forwarder throughput for AtlasAI and increased node storage IOPS to relieve writeback saturation; restarted impacted runtimes gracefully which restored service.
Permanent plan: (1) Add tenant-level forwarder rate limits and backpressure signals in Console to prevent large on-node writeback storms. (2) Add iowait-based health signal to autoscaler to isolate/evict tenants causing storage saturation. (3) Improve runbook to throttle forwarder automatically when queued_records > 50k. (4) Review default log archival-on-enable flow to use off-node buffering (S3 agent) rather than local writeback when retention increases suddenly.
